idiom_name: frozen dataclass for the old shape + explicit converter functions
implementation_notes: The window is a module: a frozen dataclass describes the legacy payload exactly as the old client sends it, dataclasses.fields() can drive generic field-by-field conversion, and explicit from_legacy()/to_legacy() functions do the mapping that actually constitutes the contract; a warnings.warn(..., DeprecationWarning) on the frozen entry points marks them for new code. Delegation, when the legacy surface is an object rather than a payload, is a hand-written __getattr__ forwarder, which is convenient but hides typos and introspection, so it is only worth it for wide frozen objects. Where the legacy contract is a wire format the standard library does not cover, a hand-written parser and encoder remain the honest implementation.
pitfalls: Money and decimals: parsing the legacy text as float invents cents the old system never had; go through Decimal and quantise at the boundary.
DeprecationWarning is ignored by default outside __main__, so the marker only works when the project enables it in tests and applications.
A __getattr__ forwarder answers to names the legacy object never had and breaks hasattr/typing; keep the frozen object explicit where the contract is small.
